title: The Man Who Hid In Plain Sight
sources: Britannica, 'Killing of Osama bin Laden': killed May 2, 2011 by SEAL Team 6 in a walled compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan; he had hidden there about six years; Abbottabad is roughly 30 miles northeast of Islamabad; four other people including his son Khalid also died; operation called Neptune Spear

Wikipedia, 'Killing of Osama bin Laden': Operation Neptune Spear launched from about 120 miles away near Jalalabad, Afghanistan; two dozen SEALs in two modified stealth Black Hawks; raid took about 40 minutes; bin Laden killed shortly before 1:00 a.m. Pakistan time; one helicopter crashed during insertion; SEALs destroyed the wreck

HISTORY.com, 'How SEAL Team Six Took Out Osama bin Laden': operation approved by President Obama; roughly 40 minutes start to finish; bin Laden found on the third floor; one Black Hawk crashed with no injuries and the mission continued

National September 11 Memorial & Museum, 'Operation Neptune Spear': two helicopters carried 23 SEALs, an interpreter and a combat dog; SEALs collected documents and electronics; the downed helicopter was blown up as a backup helicopter arrived; about 45 minutes on the ground

Britannica: the compound had no phone or internet service and trash was burned rather than collected, which helped draw CIA suspicion; CIA operatives cut power to the neighborhood as the raid began; SEALs used night vision

lines.text: Where do you hide the most wanted man on Earth?
lines.caps: Where do you *hide | the most wanted *man | on *Earth?

lines.text: Not in a cave — behind a fourteen-foot wall, in a quiet army town.

lines.text: For six years, Osama bin Laden lived in Abbottabad, near a military academy.

lines.text: No phones, no internet, trash burned in the yard. And the CIA noticed.

lines.text: Just after midnight, May second, twenty eleven — Operation Neptune Spear was a go.

lines.text: Twenty-three SEALs, an interpreter, and a combat dog.
A hundred and twenty miles from Afghanistan, in two stealth Black Hawks.

lines.text: As they came in low, the CIA cut the neighborhood's power.

lines.text: The SEALs swept in on night vision.
And the first Black Hawk slammed into the dirt.

lines.text: No one was hurt. The mission kept going.

lines.text: Forty minutes after it began, bin Laden was dead, on the third floor.

lines.text: Ten years of hiding from armies and satellites — found living in plain sight.

lines.text: The only proof of that night is a hole, where a helicopter used to be.
